channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: China, US Discuss AI, Investment as Trade Talks Continue
item.description: Chinese and US officials wrapped up their second day of talks in New York on Monday to discuss artificial intelligence, investment and trade as they sought to advance negotiations ahead of President Xi Jinping’s visit to the US this week. Bloomberg's Stephen Engle reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Australian State Bans Data Centers From Residential Areas
item.description: One of Australia’s largest states has banned the construction of data centers in residential areas and mandated that they must “bring their own renewable energy supply,” part of a slew of rules designed to tackle growing community pushback.
item.dc:creator: Ben Westcott

item.title: AI Trade Roars Back as Meta’s Personal Agent Fuels Optimism
item.description: Global AI stocks rallied as early signs of success for Meta Platforms Inc.’s new personal agent revived optimism over chip demand, bolstering the sector after a recent rough patch driven by calls for slower AI development.
item.dc:creator: Winnie Hsu

item.title: Google, Georgia Power Strike Deal to Boost Nuclear Capacity
item.description: Alphabet Inc. agreed to fund capacity increases at two nuclear plants operated by a Southern Co. subsidiary that will add about 96 megawatts of new supplies amid a data center-driven jump in electricity demand.
item.dc:creator: Julia Amann

item.title: Ligent Technologies to Debut After $727 Million in Hong Kong IPO
item.description: AI computing networks maker Ligent Technologies Inc. is set to debut on the Hong Kong stock exchange on Tuesday after raising HK$5.7 billion ($727 million) in a initial public offering, adding to this year’s stampede of companies capitalizing on the global artificial intelligence buildout.
item.dc:creator: Sangmi Cha

item.title: British Columbia Sues OpenAI Over Canada Mass Shooting Warning Failure
item.description: British Columbia filed a lawsuit in California against OpenAI, alleging it could have used ChatGPT logs to warn police and avert a mass shooting in the Canadian province earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Seal

item.title: Bitcoin Reaches Eight-Month High After Clarity Act Loss
item.description:
Bloomberg Intelligence Senior US Policy Analyst Nathan Dean discusses the Securities and Exchange Commission giving the green light for digital versions of securities to start trading in the US. This plan could reshape traditional market structure after crypto legislation failed a key Senate vote on Tuesday.
Also affecting the crypto space, Bitcoin surged past $85,000 to its highest since late-January, extending a sharp rebound as falling oil prices and a broader return of risk appetite helped cryptocurrencies move past setbacks on US crypto legislation and monetary policy. The original cryptocurrency climbed as much as 6.5% to $86,331 in New York trading, almost $10,000 above the lows touched last week after the Clarity Act stalled and the Federal Reserve raised interest rates. Even after that rebound, Bitcoin remains roughly a third below its record last October. Nathan Dean speaks with Bloomberg's Joe Mathieu on Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump-Xi Summit Puts Global AI Race in Focus
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down what to expect from the Trump-Xi summit later this week, with AI's role anticipated to be a major part of the agenda for those upcoming talks. Plus, Bloomberg reports Paramount reached a settlement with California and other states suing to block its proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. And, as data shows more disruption to US data centers, we get to the political debate with Democratic US Representative Suhas Subramanyam from Virginia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Google Takes on Apple, Microsoft With AI-Powered Laptops
item.description: Google is taking another shot at the premium laptop market with its Googlebooks, priced at $899 and built around Gemini AI and with tighter integration with Android phones. Sameer Samat, president of the Android Ecosystem at Google, explains why the company combined elements of Android and ChromeOS for the new experience and how some of the new features are designed to challenge Apple and Microsoft in the AI PC race. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Congressman Calls for National Data Center Strategy
item.description: Democratic Rep. Suhas Subramanyam of Virginia is calling for a national strategy to guide the rapid expansion of AI data centers, arguing the current state-by-state approach can leave communities bearing infrastructure costs. He discusses proposals to improve where data centers are built, measure their energy and water use, and require large electricity users to cover the grid upgrades needed to serve them. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta’s New Muse AI App Tops Charts, Draws Strong Reviews
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc.’s new artificial intelligence agent, Muse, has quickly risen to the top of mobile app charts, a sign that the social media company is gaining traction in the increasingly crowded market for consumer AI assistants.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung and Ian King

item.title: Former xAI Staffer Eyes $50 Million for Firm to Fight Deepfakes
item.description: A former xAI and Google staffer is in talks to raise roughly $50 million in seed funding for a new company focused on combating deepfakes online, according to a person familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Arroyo

item.title: Nvidia Buying an Additional $1.5 Billion in SB Energy Shares Ahead of IPO
item.description: Nvidia Corp. is buying an additional $1.5 billion in shares of SB Energy Inc., a data center provider backed by SoftBank Group Corp., ahead of that company’s US initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Nick Turner

item.title: OpenAI Pushes US to Lead Effort to Set Global Standards for AI
item.description: OpenAI is urging the US to lead an effort with other countries to set standards for cutting-edge artificial intelligence, in response to mounting concerns about the potential harms of the technology.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: How AI Could Spark the Next Copper Boom
item.description: AI data centers and power grid upgrades are quietly reshaping global copper demand. Morgan Stanley’s Amy Gower breaks down why data centers already punch above their weight, and why US tariff decisions could move copper next. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Startups Like Harvey Embrace Open Models to Cut Reliance on Anthropic, OpenAI
item.description: The $15.6 billion legal startup Harvey built its business around training AI models like OpenAI’s GPT-4 to do specialized work for lawyers. Recently, however, soaring artificial intelligence costs have nudged it to rethink its dependence on the AI giants.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence and Natasha Mascarenhas

item.title: Amazon Blocks Meta’s Muse AI Agent From Its Retail Site
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. has blocked Meta Platforms Inc.’s new artificial intelligence agent from its retail site after the social media company declined a request to remove the bot.
item.dc:creator: Matt Day and Spencer Soper

item.title: Concerned About AI Cybersecurity: Guild
item.description: Robinhood Chief Investment Officer Stephanie Guild discusses the recent concerns over AI security and competitive dynamics with Bloomberg's Dani Burger on "Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Accenture Will Help Anthropic Test AI Model Safety
item.description: Anthropic PBC is partnering with Accenture Plc to test the safety of its advanced artificial intelligence models. Evaluators from Accenture will be embedded and tasked with trying to "break" these models before they're deployed. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Smart Ring Maker Oura, Backers Seek $2.2 Billion in US IPO
item.description: Health and fitness ring-maker Oura Inc. and some of its backers are seeking to raise as much as $2.2 billion in a US initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Subrat Patnaik
